subject: Human Body
title: Mucus Membranes
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mucus Membranes usable.

hook.text: Your nose produces about a liter of mucus daily. Most of it slides down your throat unnoticed. That's by design.

buildup.text: Mucus lines the airways, gut, and reproductive tract. It traps dust, bacteria, and viruses in a sticky film.

discovery.text: Tiny hair-like cilia beat in waves, pushing contaminated mucus toward exits: throat, nose, or stomach acid.

twist.text: Smoking paralyzes cilia. Without them, mucus pools and infections rise. That's why smokers cough more often.

climax.text: Mucus is a conveyor belt of defense, constantly trapping and removing threats before they reach vulnerable tissue.

punchline.text: Mucus is gross but brilliant. It traps what shouldn't enter.

quiz.question: What role do cilia play in mucus defense?
options: They beat in waves to push contaminated mucus out
They produce mucus when triggered by allergens
